> 


You may have better luck on the RStudio mailing lists. RStudio is not R, so THEy may give you better idea about what is RStudio doing that would clash with multi-threaded system like Java.

BTW: System.out is just stdio by default - it is typically ignored by R, you can try using R console I/O instead if you want output in R, .e.g, see org.rosuda.JRI.RConsoleOutputStream

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Constructing RConsoleOutputStream
messages.body_plain:
On Feb 2, 2015, at 1:56 AM, Ralph Fehrer <ralphfehrer at gmail.com> wrote:

> Just tried to construct an ROutputStream in my R-Studio script, as
> recommended in the docu.
> 
> I got this far without errors:
> 
> rengine <- .jnew("org/rosuda/JRI/Rengine")
> 
> Then I tried the following variations to create an RConsoleOutputStream,
> without success:
> 
> printStream <- .jnew("org/rosuda/JRI/RConsoleOutputStream",rengine,0)
> printStream <- .jnew("org/rosuda/JRI/RConsoleOutputStream",c(rengine,0))
> 
> The correct constructor could not be inferred, from the list of parameters I
> provided. 
> 
> What am I doing wrong?
> 

First, the way to start the JRI engine is .jengine(). Second, the signature requires an integer, not double (if you're not sure, use J() high-level API instead), so together:

e <- .jengine(TRUE)
printStream <- .jnew("org/rosuda/JRI/RConsoleOutputStream",e,0L)

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello;

I'm using the latest java Rserve client (fresh jars downloaded off 
http://rforge.net/Rserve/files/ which I assume to be version 1.8-1) to 
connect to a version 1.8-1 server; I'm trying to send a rather large 
command (about 50MB string) to voidEvalDetach and I'm getting an 
exception from the client:

[ERROR] : Failure executing job 
edu.dfci.cccb.mev.cluster.domain.IntegratedClusteringTest$H@395771a2
org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException: detached void eval failed
	at 
org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection.voidEvalDetach(RConnection.java:194)
	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.execute(R.java:200)
	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.access$0(R.java:140)
	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R$2.run(R.java:121)
	at 
java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1110)
	at 
java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:603)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:722)
java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 14956321
	at org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.protocol.RTalk.request(RTalk.java:245)
	at 
org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection.voidEvalDetach(RConnection.java:192)
	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.execute(R.java:200)
	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.access$0(R.java:140)
	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R$2.run(R.java:121)
	at 
java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1110)
	at 
java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:603)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:722)

I've tried setting the maxinbuffer on the server to 4194304 which should 
be large enough, but this obviously happens before the command ever gets 
there. Is it possible to fix this with client configuration?

I'm trying to write a framework using Rserve from within a web 
application, I've found the most straight forward way to send context 
back and forth would be through json strings which is why the message is 
so long - I'm encoding a roughly 30k X 50 data frame in json and sending 
it within the command which is then parsed on the R slave side by 
jsonlite. Everything functions fine with a 10K X 50 data frame, the 
issue appears at about 16MB command size.

I suppose I could start sending the json as files and read it on the 
slave, which is probably what I should do anyway, but I was hoping I 
could go ahead as is for a quick proof of concept.

I'm sorry if this already came up at some point, I couldn't find the 
archives for the list.

Thank you,
Lev.

On Feb 4, 2015, at 4:14 PM, levk <levk at jimmy.harvard.edu> wrote:

> Hello;
> 
> I'm using the latest java Rserve client (fresh jars downloaded off http://rforge.net/Rserve/files/ which I assume to be version 1.8-1) to connect to a version 1.8-1 server; I'm trying to send a rather large command (about 50MB string) to voidEvalDetach and I'm getting an exception from the client:
> 
> [ERROR] : Failure executing job edu.dfci.cccb.mev.cluster.domain.IntegratedClusteringTest$H@395771a2
> org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException: detached void eval failed
> 	at org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection.voidEvalDetach(RConnection.java:194)
> 	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.execute(R.java:200)
> 	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.access$0(R.java:140)
> 	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R$2.run(R.java:121)
> 	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1110)
> 	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:603)
> 	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:722)
> java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 14956321
> 	at org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.protocol.RTalk.request(RTalk.java:245)
> 	at org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection.voidEvalDetach(RConnection.java:192)
> 	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.execute(R.java:200)
> 	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R.access$0(R.java:140)
> 	at edu.dfci.cccb.mev.common.domain.jobs.r.R$2.run(R.java:121)
> 	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1110)
> 	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:603)
> 	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:722)
> 
> I've tried setting the maxinbuffer on the server to 4194304 which should be large enough, but this obviously happens before the command ever gets there. Is it possible to fix this with client configuration?
> 
> I'm trying to write a framework using Rserve from within a web application, I've found the most straight forward way to send context back and forth would be through json strings which is why the message is so long - I'm encoding a roughly 30k X 50 data frame in json and sending it within the command which is then parsed on the R slave side by jsonlite. Everything functions fine with a 10K X 50 data frame, the issue appears at about 16MB command size.
> 

Yes, evals in the Java client don't support large packets for strings (in fact none of the APIs  that are special wrappers for strings do), so there is a 16MB limit to what you can evaluate.

However, it's highly inefficient and error-prone to do it that way, because you have to go through the R parser. You should rather use either assign(String, REXP) to assign the long string to variable or eval(REXP, REXP, false) to call a function directly with that long string. Both support large objects (as long as you use REXPString() and *not* the String wrappers), so you don't have the 24-bit limit. In general, it's a very bad idea to pass strings via the parser since you'll get into the quoting hell :).

So although it wouldn't be hard to add large packet support to the Java client where immediate string conversion is provided, I would still advise against using it that way.

Cheers,
Simon
